title: A Superfluid at All Temperatures
abstract: We construct unitary, local, 3+1-dimensional conformal field theories with finitely many fields whose thermal state breaks a continuous global symmetry at every temperature. They are finite-$N$ versions of the Chaudhuri--Choi--Rabinovici theories, whose planar circle of fixed points has an ordered arc. The circle is lifted at order $1/N^2$, and an infinite family of fixed points on this arc reaches arbitrarily weak coupling, where the superfluid is under parametric control. We also show that weakly gauging the symmetry gives a superconductor over an exponential range of temperatures.
summary: This paper constructs a family of quantum field theories that exhibit superfluidity at every temperature by controlling the symmetry breaking mechanism through the renormalization group flow. By analyzing $ eta$-functions in the large-$N$ limit with finite-$N$ corrections, the authors prove the existence of an infinite family of such theories, which also manifest superconductivity when coupled to electromagnetism.
main_problem: The authors aim to construct unitary, local, 3+1-dimensional conformal field theories whose thermal state spontaneously breaks a continuous global symmetry at every temperature.
main_result: They constructed an infinite family of such theories where the superfluid nature of the thermal state is under parametric perturbative control, and weakly gauging the symmetry yields a superconductor over an exponential temperature range.
method: The analysis involves calculating and analyzing $ eta$-functions up to two loops, comparing the planar limit ($N 	o \infty$) to finite-$N$ corrections ($1/N^2$), and determining fixed points by solving $ eta^{(1)}_	heta = 0$.

key_observables: Superfluid stiffness, Meissner mass ($m_M$), thermal free energy density ($\Delta f^*$), and the existence of ordered fixed points.
important_parameters: The large-$N$ limit, finite-$N$ corrections ($1/N^2$), and the coupling constants $\lambda^*_i$ which can be driven to arbitrarily weak values.
main_assumptions: The theories are assumed to be unitary, local, and possess finitely many fields. The analysis relies on systematic perturbative expansions in $1/N^2$ and $ ar{\lambda}$.

paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the $ eta$-functions in the large-$N$ limit, identifies the ordered arc of fixed points, incorporates finite-$N$ corrections via a lift, and finally demonstrates the existence of an infinite family of theories exhibiting superfluidity and superconductivity.
why_interesting: The rigorous construction of a superfluid state at all temperatures in a controlled QFT framework is highly relevant to understanding exotic phases of matter, such as those found in condensed matter systems or in the context of quantum field theory renormalization group flow.
